module: Development tool that measures a vehicle's suspension frequency. It shows an ImGui window "Suspension Frequency Tester": for two nodes (front axle 279, rear axle 425 by default) it reads the z height every frame and feeds it into 1000 frequency detection filters (newFreqExists) between 0.5 Hz and 5 Hz, then compares against categories (Too Soft 0.9 Hz, Luxury 1.1, Average 1.2, Sporty 1.4, Rally 1.8, Racetrack 2.2, Aero-Critical 5.0). The file explains the usage: put the car on ice, remove the damping, then run extensions.suspensionFrequencyTester.run() from the console.
notes: Node ids 279 and 425 are hard-coded for one specific vehicle; they can be changed in the window ('Front axle node ID' / 'Rear axle node ID' fields).
The module reads imgui when it loads (ui_imgui): it must therefore only be loaded on the GE side with the imgui interface available.
The table's 'm/Hz' display is an integral of amplitudes divided by the band width in Hz (formatted as an integer by %i).
The header comment says extensions.suspensionFrequencyTester.run(); the automatic page says require(...): both assume the module is loaded as an extension.

onUpdate.desc: Hook called every frame by the extension system: draws the window if it is open, then (if a player vehicle exists) updates for each node the amplitudes of all frequency filters from the node's z position (veh:getNodePositionXYZ) and dtSim.

dtSim.desc: Simulated frame duration (s), passed to the filters.

run.desc: Opens the window and resets the amplitudes and frequency filters of each node to start a new measurement.
